cells.reason: EU 2023/915 Annex I lead row 'cephalopods' (0.30 mg/kg wet weight, the animal without viscera) covers octopus, squid and cuttlefish sold fresh or frozen; wet-weight edible-portion content is the cell's as-consumed content basis, and the regulation has applied since 25 May 2023 (the 0.30 value dates from Reg. 2015/1005, carried into 2023/915). No non-gated same-basis Pb row is stricter: every other cephalopod or mollusc row in the register (CR, PA, GY, PY and MERCOSUR 12/11, GSO 193, India FSSAI, Fiji, Vietnam, Hong Kong 'aquatic animals other than fish, crustaceans and bivalve molluscs', China GB 2762-2025, Mexico NOM-242, AU-NZ Schedule 19, Singapore 'fish, crustaceans and molluscs') sits at 1000 to 2000 ug/kg, and the only rows at or below 300 are gated (Israel FCS 2016 'octopus and squid' 300 superseded; Guyana 25 ppb quarantined) or scoped to fish muscle rather than cephalopods.

EU 2023/915 cadmium row 'cephalopods' (1.0 mg/kg wet weight, without viscera) covers the product on the cell's content basis and the instrument is in force. Register rows at 50 to 500 ug/kg are fish-muscle rows or residual rows displaced by a specific cephalopod or mollusc row in the same instrument (Vietnam 'aquatic products' 50 versus its 'cephalopod mollusks' 2000; Mexico 'other fishery products' 500 versus its 'molluscs' 2000; Singapore 'other food' 200 versus its 'molluscs or dried mushrooms' 1000; CR, PA, GY, Fiji, GSO, Morocco, Bosnia and China fish-muscle rows versus their own cephalopod rows), and Uruguay's residual 'solid foods in general except categories with particular limits' 200 yields to the MERCOSUR 12/11 cephalopod limit (2000) that applies in states-party territory. Costa Rica, Guyana, Fiji and Singapore cephalopod or mollusc rows equal 1000; none is stricter.

Paraguay Decree 1335/2019, the national incorporation of MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/11, carries the arsenic-table row 'cephalopod molluscs' 1 mg/kg on 'product as offered to the consumer'; the page records it as total arsenic (the table says arsenic without inorganic speciation), a content ML that covers the product form and has been in force since the decree of 20 February 2019. Equal 1000 ug/kg total-arsenic rows cover the same product in AU-NZ Schedule 19 ('molluscs'), Singapore ('fish, crustaceans and molluscs'), MERCOSUR 12/11 itself and Uruguay's general solid-food limit, so nothing non-gated on the same basis is stricter; Guyana's 200 ppb row is quarantined and Israel FCS 2016 'seafood' 1000 is superseded. The EU 2025/1891 cephalopod value of 0.050 mg/kg is inorganic arsenic, a different analyte, and is not a same-analyte candidate.

EU 2023/915 Annex I 3.3.1.3 (the tier inserted by Reg. 2022/617) names 'cephalopods' and 'marine gastropods' expressly in the 0.30 mg/kg wet-weight total-mercury tier; edible-portion wet weight is the cell's content basis and the tier has applied since 3 May 2022. Every other cephalopod mercury row is equal or looser (Bosnia 3.3.3 mirror 300; MERCOSUR and Paraguay 'cephalopod molluscs' 500; CR, GY, Panama and India 500; Hong Kong 'aquatic animals other than fish' 500; Thailand 'other marine animals or plants' MeHg 500), so no stricter same-basis row is missing. Noted but not listed as a candidate: Singapore reg 31(3)(d) 'other food' 0.05 ppm would reach cephalopods only if they are not 'fish or fish product' under 31(3)(b), a definition the register and page do not settle, and Uruguay's residual 50 ug/kg general-food row yields to the MERCOSUR cephalopod limit.

The anchor's 0.30 mg/kg tier (Annex I 3.3.1.3) covers carp (Cyprinidae), salmon and trout (Salmo and Oncorhynchus, excluding Salmo trutta) and the Pangasius catfishes (basa, striped catfish, Mekong giant catfish), but it does not list tilapia (Oreochromis) or the Ictalurid channel catfish that 'catfish' means in the North American market, and it excludes brown trout; those species fall under 3.3.1.1 'muscle meat of fish' at 0.50 mg/kg wet weight. A cell whose product form is defined as 'tilapia, catfish, trout, carp' therefore cannot carry 300 as a firm sovereign number for the whole form: 300 is protective (no in-scope EU value is stricter) but for tilapia, channel catfish and brown trout it is a precautionary tightening of a 500 ug/kg ML, not regulatory alignment, so the category needs a species split or an explicit precautionary tag for the 500-tier species. No stricter non-gated same-basis row was found (Singapore 'other fish or fish product' 500, Uruguay fish muscle 500, MERCOSUR and Paraguay 'fish except predators' 500, Fiji, India, Guyana, CR and Panama 500); Thailand 414's residual total-mercury 'food other than the listed total-mercury categories' 0.02 mg/kg row is flagged because non-marine non-predatory fish have no methylmercury row there and the register scope wording leaves its reach undecided.

Every species the cell names is on the EU Annex I 3.3.1.3 0.30 mg/kg wet-weight list for muscle meat: sardine or pilchard (Sardina, Sardinops, Sardinella, Dussumieria), anchovy (Engraulis), salmon (Salmo and Oncorhynchus), Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua), Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus) and mackerel (Scomber); the basis matches and the tier has applied since 3 May 2022. No non-gated same-basis tHg row is stricter (Singapore 'other fish or fish product' 500, Uruguay fish muscle 500, MERCOSUR and Paraguay 500, CR, Panama, Guyana, Fiji, India and AU-NZ 500; Bosnia mirrors 300). The cell's scope must be read as the 3.3.1.3 species list rather than 'non-predatory' generally: Pacific cod, Pacific herring, Trachurus and Scomberomorus mackerels, haddock, hake, sea bass, sea bream and most flatfish other than common dab, European flounder, plaice and sole sit at 3.3.1.1's 500 ug/kg.

Bounded cell: methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury, and the parent tHg cell rests on a firm sovereign number, EU 2023/915 Annex I 3.3.1.3 'cephalopods' 0.30 mg/kg wet weight, in force since 3 May 2022. No non-gated methylmercury row on a content basis is stricter than 300 for cephalopods (Thailand 'other marine animals or plants' 500, China GB 2762-2025 'aquatic animals and their products' 500, FDA CPG 540.600 action level 1000), so the 300 bound stands.

Bounded by the parent tHg cell, whose anchor is refuted for this product form: EU 3.3.1.3 covers carp, Salmo and Oncorhynchus trout and the Pangasius catfishes but places tilapia, Ictalurid channel catfish and brown trout under 3.3.1.1 at 0.50 mg/kg, so the parent is not a firm sovereign number for every species the cell names. The 300 bound remains protective and no methylmercury row is stricter (Philippines, Vietnam, Hong Kong and Trinidad non-predatory fish 500, China 500, FDA 1000), but the cell inherits the parent's species-split or precautionary-tag fix.

Bounded cell: the parent tHg number is a firm sovereign value, EU 2023/915 Annex I 3.3.1.3 at 0.30 mg/kg wet weight for the named sardine, anchovy, salmon, Atlantic cod, Atlantic herring and Scomber mackerel muscle meat, in force. No non-gated methylmercury row is stricter than 300 for these species (Philippines 'fish' 500, Vietnam 'fish excluding carnivorous fish' 500, Hong Kong 'fish other than those specified' 500, Trinidad 'all fish except predatory fish' 500, Mexico 'other fishery products' 500, China 500, FDA 1000), so MeHg is bounded at 300 subject to the same 3.3.1.3 species-list reading as the parent.

Product form: cephalopods (octopus, squid, cuttlefish; not canned). The anchor's scope, 'canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products', does not reach a product the cell defines as not canned, and it is not the nearest same-basis sovereign instrument: the register holds direct residual content rows that cover any fresh or frozen food, Singapore Food Regulations reg 31(4) 'any food' 250 ppm (sg_foodregs_2026_any_food_sn_250000, consolidation in force 30 January 2026), Thailand MOPH 414 'foods other than the listed tin categories' 250 mg/kg (th_moph414_2020_sn_food_other_250000) and Uruguay RBN 'foods in general except categories with particular limits' 250 mg/kg (uy_rbn_general_sn_foods_250mgkg), all 250000 ug/kg. Those direct rows are looser than the 200000 read-across, so the published number sits below every applicable ML and no stricter same-basis candidate exists, but the provenance is wrong: the cell should either cite the direct residual rows as a gov cell (250000) or disclose 200000 as a precautionary value chosen below them. If a canned analog is nevertheless retained, the product-nearer canned rows are the canned fishery rows (MX NOM-242 'canned fishery products only' 100 mg/kg wet weight, CR RTCR 409 and India FSSAI canned fish 200 mg/kg), of which MX at 100000 is strictest, so the EU general canned-foods row is neither the direct instrument nor the nearest canned analog.
